title: Relative product theorem
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ and $k=\overline{k_0}$. Fix a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$. Put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] for these parameters, with its categories $D^b_{ctf}(-,\Lambda)$, derived tensor and pullback, compact-support image, and the supplied axioms (A1)--(A6). Let $B$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $f:X\to B$, $g:Y\to B$ separated finite type, $\pi_X,\pi_Y$ the
projections of $X\times_BY$ (so $f\times_Bg=g\circ \pi_Y$), and put $K\boxtimes L=\pi_X^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda \pi_Y^*L$ for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$.
Define the canonical map as the composite of the inverse of the
composition isomorphism $Rg_!R\pi_{Y!}\cong R(f\times_Bg)_!$ of (A4), the inverse
of the projection transformation of [def-sf-pf] for $\pi_Y$ at $(\pi_X^*K,L)$, the
inverse of the base-change exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!K\to R\pi_{Y!}L\pi_X^*K$ of (A2), the symmetry of
$\otimes^L_\Lambda$, and the inverse of the projection transformation for $g$
at $(L,Rf_!K)$ followed by the symmetry, i.e. of the four steps of the proof
below (its coherence — symmetry, triple products, base change, projection
formula — is the separate coherence lemma for the relative product). Then this
canonical map

$$
R(f\times_Bg)_!\bigl(K\boxtimes L\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L
$$

is an isomorphism, natural in $K$ and $L$, compatible with base change
$b:B'\to B$ for $B'$ separated of finite type over $k$, finite reduction, scalar extension, and with the
identifications $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$. For $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$
and closed immersions $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_W:W\hookrightarrow Y$,
it gives the compact-support product on the closed subschemes:

$$
R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)\otimes^L_\Lambda R\Gamma_c(W,i_W^*L)
\cong R\Gamma_c(Z\times_kW,(i_Z\times i_W)^*(K\boxtimes L)).
$$

This is cohomology of the restrictions to the closed subschemes.
Cohomology with supports $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)=R\Gamma(Z,Ri_Z^!K)$ is a different
object from $R\Gamma_c(Z,i_Z^*K)$. The absolute supports formula is treated separately in the purity and duality chapters. Over a general base $B$ the supports version
fails, so only the compact-support form is stated relatively.

proof.text: Work in the axiomatized six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum]; this proof uses its explicitly supplied (A2)--(A5), not a claim that defining concrete operations proves those axioms. Put $T=X\times_BY$ and $h=g\pi_Y=f\pi_X$. The base-change theorem [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] gives that $\pi_X,\pi_Y$ are separated of finite type. For composition, the finite affine covers in the finite-type definition compose, and generators for $C$ over $A$ are the images of generators for $B/A$ together with generators for $C/B$. Separatedness of a composite follows because its diagonal is the composite of the diagonal of the first map and a base change of the diagonal of the second; both are closed immersions by the cited closed-immersion base-change and composition statements. Thus $h=g\pi_Y$ is also separated of finite type. The finite-Tor typing needed below is $L\pi_X^*K,L\pi_Y^*L\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ and $Rf_!K\in D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$: at finite coefficients these are precisely clauses (i), (iv) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability]; at the integral and field stages the datum supplies the operations on the stated finite-Tor categories, with the coefficient-passage conventions of that stability statement. No exceptional-image or duality clause of stability is used. Clause (ii) of [thm-sf-ctf-stability] also puts the exterior tensor input in the finite-Tor category. For the finite witnessed composition and the concrete exchange-pasting statements used below, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies an etale-origin witness for each bounded constructible finite-coefficient input. At the integral stage apply this to every constructible finite reduction in the specified derived-complete construction; at the rational and algebraically closed stages use the integral presentation and a common finite coefficient stage. These are the completed and transported domains of [fix-lem-exchanges], not discrete non-torsion etale coefficient categories.

source.place: Proof, typing before (1) and the explanation after (4)

proof.text: Apply the inverse composition isomorphism of (A4) at $L\pi_X^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\pi_Y^*L$. Its source is $Rh_!(K\boxtimes L)$ and its target is $Rg_!R\pi_{Y!}(L\pi_X^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\pi_Y^*L)$. At the finite witnessed pro-etale level this is the canonical $\alpha_{g,\pi_Y}^{-1}$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]; at other stages use its supplied composition isomorphism (A4).

The inverse projection transformation $\operatorname{PF}_{\pi_Y,L\pi_X^*K,L}^{-1}$ sends $R\pi_{Y!}(L\pi_X^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\pi_Y^*L)$ to $R\pi_{Y!}L\pi_X^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda L$. Its type is exactly [def-sf-pf], and its invertibility is (A3), concretely the all-coefficient projection formula [fix-prop-projection-formula]. Apply $Rg_!$ to this inverse. No symmetry is inserted at this step.

The Cartesian square $T\xrightarrow{\pi_X}X$, $T\xrightarrow{\pi_Y}Y$, $X\xrightarrow{f}B$, $Y\xrightarrow{g}B$ has exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!:Lg^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_{Y!}L\pi_X^*K$ by (A2). Tensor its inverse with $1_L$ and apply $Rg_!$. This gives $Rg_!(Lg^*Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L)$. Tensor symmetry then gives $Rg_!(L\otimes^L_\Lambda Lg^*Rf_!K)$.

Apply $\operatorname{PF}_{g,L,Rf_!K}^{-1}$ to the preceding object. Step 1 checked its second variable is in the finite-Tor domain. This gives $Rg_!L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rf_!K$, and tensor symmetry gives $Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda Rg_!L$. We have used exactly the arrows defining the canonical map in the statement. Each is an isomorphism, so their composite is an isomorphism.

Each factor is natural in both inputs: the composition and exchange are natural transformations and the two projection maps are natural by [fix-prop-projection-formula] and [prop-sf-pf-coherence]. The inverse of an invertible natural transformation is natural, and tensoring and applying a functor preserve naturality, so their composite is natural. The coefficient comparison squares for its factors commute by (A5) and projection coherence; composing these squares proves finite-reduction and scalar-extension compatibility. For proper morphisms replace $R(-)_!$ by $R(-)_*$ through the (A4) identification; projection coherence identifies the projection factor with the direct-image factor and (A5) identifies the remaining coefficient comparisons, giving the asserted proper identification. At finite coefficients [cor-cbc-proper-coincidence] says exactly that the compact-support exchange under the canonical proper identification is the proper-base-change exchange; at higher stages use its coefficient-passage compatibility supplied by (A5). Thus the proper comparison is also the specified exchange comparison, not an arbitrary isomorphism between the two functors.

Let $b:B'\to B$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and use primes for all its base changes, with $v:Y'\to Y$, $u:X'\to X$, and $w:T'\to T$. Use the monoidal pullback comparison to identify $Lw^*(K\boxtimes L)$ with $Lu^*K\boxtimes Lv^*L$. The exchange pasting equations of [fix-lem-exchanges] identify the square for $Lb^*\alpha_{g,\pi_Y}^{-1}$ with that for $\alpha_{g',\pi_Y'}^{-1}$. The base-change square of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] for $\pi_Y$ along $v$, read backwards, identifies the inverse first projection factors. The exchange pasting equations identify the exchanged $R\pi_{Y!}L\pi_X^*K$ factors. The same projection-coherence square for $g$ along $b$, again read backwards, identifies the final inverse projection factors. Naturality of tensor symmetry and the monoidal pullback comparison identifies the two symmetry factors. Compose these commuting squares in the order of steps 2--5: the result is exactly the square comparing $Lb^*$ of the stated composite to the composite for $(f',g',Lu^*K,Lv^*L)$ through the exchanges for $f,g,h$. This proves the claimed base-change compatibility without invoking the later relative-product coherence lemma.

Put $B=s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and let $i_Z:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $i_W:W\hookrightarrow Y$ be closed immersions. The closed-immersion properness statement makes $i_Z,i_W$ separated of finite type, and the composition argument of step 1 makes their structure maps separated of finite type, and pullback stability puts $Li_Z^*K,Li_W^*L$ in the finite-Tor domains. Apply the construction of steps 1--5 to these two schemes. If $r:Z\times_kW\to X\times_kY$ is the product immersion, with projections $\pi'_X,\pi'_Y$, monoidality and pullback composition give
$$Lr^*(L\pi_X^*K\otimes^L L\pi_Y^*L)\cong L(\pi_X r)^*K\otimes^L L(\pi_Y r)^*L
\cong L\pi'_X^*Li_Z^*K\otimes^L L\pi'_Y^*Li_W^*L,$$
since $\pi_X r=i_Z\pi'_X$ and $\pi_Y r=i_W\pi'_Y$. Thus the input is precisely $r^*(K\boxtimes L)$, rather than an extraordinary restriction or a supported complex.

Invert that specialized isomorphism and apply $\operatorname{Fib}_s$. By [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology], the three compact-support direct images become the corresponding $R\Gamma_c$ complexes. The canonical tensor comparison of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] identifies the fibre of the tensor product with the tensor product of the two fibres. The resulting isomorphism is exactly the displayed closed-subscheme compact-support product formula. This argument uses restrictions $Li_Z^*,Li_W^*$; it makes no assertion about the distinct cohomology-with-support functor of [def-pur-support-cohomology].

proof.text:
The operations are those of [def-sf-datum] and [def-sf-pf],
cohomology with supports has its separate meaning in
[def-pur-support-cohomology].
Step 1: by (A4), $R(f\times_Bg)_!=Rg_!\circ Rq_!$, so
$R(f\times_Bg)_!(K\boxtimes L)=Rg_!\bigl(Rq_!(q^*L\otimes^L_\Lambda p^*K)\bigr)$. Step 2: the projection formula (A3) for $q$, whose target is
$Y$, gives $Rq_!(q^*L\otimes^L p^*K)\cong L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rq_!(p^*K)$.
Step 3: base change (A2) for the Cartesian square with $p,q,f,g$ gives
$Rq_!(p^*K)\cong Lg^*Rf_!K$. Step 4: applying the projection formula to
$g$ with first variable $L$ and second variable $Rf_!K$ gives
$Rg_!\bigl(L\otimes^L_\Lambda Lg^*Rf_!K\bigr)\cong Rg_!L\otimes^L_\Lambda Rf_!K$, which is the displayed isomorphism. Step 5:
apply the same formula to the separated finite-type morphisms
$Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $W\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the
pullbacks $i_Z^*K,i_W^*L$. Pullback preserves their finite-Tor
hypotheses, and the exterior product is the pullback of $K\boxtimes L$.
This proves the claimed compact-support formula on the closed subschemes.
